title: Bluetooth re-enables
line: Bluetooth that you turned off no longer turns itself back on after resume.
explanation: Every time an adapter appears (at login, and again when it re-registers after resume or a firmware reset), bluedevil's kded restores its powered state one second later in DeviceMonitor::restoreAdapter(). That read the saved state with a default of on, and since Bluetooth being disabled clears the saved adapter states, an adapter re-appearing while Bluetooth was off got powered back on. The 2025 fix (76da3998) only covered restoreState(), not this path. Now restoreAdapter() only sets the powered state when one was saved for that adapter, like restoreState().

commits.message:
kded: don't power on adapters with no saved state when they appear

When an adapter showed up, for example again after resume, its powered
state was restored with a default of on, so Bluetooth that the user had
disabled came back. Only restore it when a state was saved for it.

BUG: 507836

patches.diff:
From 117610e52a24f8b824f1efd0c518c9c7ab28a24d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 02:33:08 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] kded: don't power on adapters with no saved state when they
 appear

When an adapter showed up, for example again after resume, its powered
state was restored with a default of on, so Bluetooth that the user had
disabled came back. Only restore it when a state was saved for it.

BUG: 507836
---
 src/kded/devicemonitor.cpp | 5 ++++-
 1 file changed, 4 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/src/kded/devicemonitor.cpp b/src/kded/devicemonitor.cpp
index 1de54443..f78fc2b8 100644
--- a/src/kded/devicemonitor.cpp
+++ b/src/kded/devicemonitor.cpp
@@ -216,7 +216,10 @@ void DeviceMonitor::restoreAdapter(BluezQt::AdapterPtr adapter)
     KConfigGroup adaptersGroup = GlobalSettings::self()->config()->group("Adapters");
 
     const QString &key = QStringLiteral("%1_powered").arg(adapter->address());
-    adapter->setPowered(adaptersGroup.readEntry<bool>(key, true));
+
+    if (adaptersGroup.hasKey(key)) {
+        adapter->setPowered(adaptersGroup.readEntry<bool>(key, true));
+    }
 }
 
 void DeviceMonitor::clearPlaces()
